tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Diagnose and review...', 'Use this skill when...'), lists explicit, concrete trigger contexts (truncated responses, judge score swings, RAG eval failures, SageMaker Nova recipe failures, model comparison questions, etc.) covering diverse phrasings users might use, and focuses on user-facing symptoms/goals rather than internal implementation. While long, the length is justified by the breadth of trigger scenarios it needs to disambiguate, and it remains a single coherent paragraph without wandering into internal mechanics beyond brief mentions (check-ids, read-only).
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when answers got worse or a model may hallucinate more, responses are cut off or end on max_tokens, the same prompt gives different answers, a Bedrock CreateEvaluationJob or a Bedrock RAG evaluation job for a knowledge base fails or needs interpreting..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and almost entirely devoted to domain-specific, non-obvious conventions (check-ids, severity catalog, API quirks, routing rules) rather than explaining general concepts the agent would already know.
tests.evidence: 'A shift from end_turn (natural completion) toward max_tokens (truncation) means outputs are being cut off' — this is domain-specific, not generic AI knowledge explained at length.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Large reference data (full check catalog, metrics/log schemas, API quirks, known causes) is kept in references/ files and only summarized/linked in the body; the body itself doesn't embed large lookup tables except a short severity table and a small routing table, which are appropriately sized and decision-critical per the skill's own Guardrail 7.
tests.evidence: 'Walk [checks-evaluation.md](references/checks-evaluation.md) for the path you are on, applying each detection rule.' — detailed catalog content is offloaded, not duplicated inline.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked with a markdown link format in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by explicit load-when guidance throughout the body.
tests.evidence: '[checks-evaluation.md](references/checks-evaluation.md) (load it before assigning any check-id or severity)' and '[metrics-and-logs.md](references/metrics-and-logs.md) (load before any log query or metric read)'.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.
tests.evidence: '[finish-reason-analysis.md](references/finish-reason-analysis.md)' is a relative path format used consistently.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, high-stakes operations (read-only guardrails, finish-reason measurement rules, output contract) are given exact prescriptive language, while investigatory judgment (deciding which path, synthesizing findings) is left flexible with rationale given.
tests.evidence: 'Never call a mutating API — in particular CreateEvaluationJob, StopEvaluationJob...' is prescriptive for a fragile safety rule, while 'A question can take more than one path; say which' leaves room for judgment.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple evaluation paths exist, the skill doesn't present them as an undifferentiated menu — it names them explicitly and gives rules to select among them (service check, routing table), rather than leaving choice ambiguous.
tests.evidence: 'Decide which service ran it first (Step 1)' with explicit disambiguation logic — this is decision guidance, not an equal-options menu, since paths are determined by the actual job type, not left as an agent choice.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigation procedure (steps 1-5, routing table, check catalog application) applicable to any model/job, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: 'Step 1: Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support' through 'Step 5: Synthesize' describes a reusable procedure for any evaluation question.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has extensive gotchas content, both inline ('Common wrong answers') and in a dedicated references/known-causes.md and api-quirks.md, covering concrete non-obvious pitfalls.
tests.evidence: '"ListEvaluationJobs" is empty, so no evaluation has ever run — CRITICAL.' Bedrock evaluation is region-gated... confirm regional support first and report INFO/advisory, not LLM-EVAL-001'.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: Output templates exist in assets/ for both Bedrock and SageMaker report paths, and an inline output contract is specified, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.
tests.evidence: 'load [evaluation-report-template.md](assets/evaluation-report-template.md) for the Bedrock path and the posture review, and [sagemaker-evaluation-report-template.md](assets/sagemaker-evaluation-report-template.md)'.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The only inline template-like content is the short Findings block format (a few lines), well under 20 lines; larger report templates are properly offloaded to assets/.
tests.evidence: 'Findings\n<check-id> (<SEVERITY>) — ... — <doc URL>' is a short, few-line inline template.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three asset files are linked in the body with markdown links.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each asset link includes explicit guidance on when to load it.
tests.evidence: '[delegation-payload.json](assets/delegation-payload.json) is that prompt, finished (load when delegating evidence-gathering)' and 'load [evaluation-report-template.md](assets/evaluation-report-template.md) for the Bedrock path and the posture review'.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: All asset references use relative paths from the skill root with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural Investigation Procedure section uses the required checkbox checklist format with 'Step N:' naming, and detailed sections below reference the same step numbers (e.g., '### Step 1 — Understand the question...').
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support' ... '### Step 1 — Understand the question, pick the path and confirm regional support'.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own draft output before presenting, covering multiple concrete validation checks.
tests.evidence: '## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' with items like 'Scan the draft for an upgraded negative, sentence by sentence' and 'No unqualified negative survives in the prose.'
